correctness.rationale: Writing the singleton probabilities as \(F_i=P_0 o_i\), equality of a nonzero fingerprint forces the odds vectors onto one positive ray. Along that ray the common scale is \(h(u)=u/\prod_j(1+ur_j)\) and \(h'(u)/h(u)=(1-\sum_j p_j(u))/u\), so the scale is strictly increasing up to the unique sum-one point. This proves injectivity on \(\sum p_i\le1\). The homogeneous profile \(u(1-u)^{n-1}\) has its unique maximum at \(1/n\), proving the exact cube threshold and the two-to-one fold above it. At the boundary the fingerprint change is quadratic in a homogeneous perturbation while a one-coordinate marginal gives a linear total-variation lower bound, so no uniform Lipschitz TV upper bound exists. Independent bounded numerical checks reproduced the fold and the boundary blow-up for dimensions two through eight.
